prompt:
Wide editorial illustration of a creative technology team working simultaneously at night. 16:9 panoramic format. Painterly, editorial brushwork with visible grain — the quality of a commissioned magazine illustration, not photorealistic, not flat-design, not animated.

COMPOSITION:
A long studio space at night or late evening. The overhead lights are dimmed or off — the room is lit almost entirely by the glow of individual workstation screens. Six people are at their stations across the width of the frame, each completely absorbed in their own task. The visual rhythm is: person / glow / dark gap / person / glow — the team in separate pools of light, all moving at once.

THE PEOPLE (left to right):

1. Far left — Ethan (security): a white man, late thirties, short dark hair, subtle beard-stubble, dark zip-collar jacket. Seated at the far left, facing dual monitors that cast a cool green-tinted glow on his face (suggesting terminal / code). His expression is watchful, controlled. The corner he occupies is slightly darker than the rest of the room. (The green terminal glow is the primary light on his face — the rest of his corner is dark.)

2. Center-left — Indy (researcher): a white man in his mid-forties, wavy medium-length light brown hair with some grey, green henley shirt. Seated to Claude's left, leaning forward toward a laptop screen. His desk has colorful sticky notes, a large ceramic mug, and a small stack of open books. His expression is intent — tracking something, mid-thought. (Laptop screen illuminates him from below and in front; the sticky notes catch light; a desk lamp adds a small warm halo.)

3. CENTER (focal anchor) — The director: a Black man in his forties, close-cropped hair, navy cardigan over a light collared shirt. Seated at center of the long shared desk, body turned slightly toward the viewer, gaze down on an open notebook filled with flowing connection diagrams — arrows linking nodes — the sketch of a system being built. Calm, fully absorbed. A few stacked books behind him on a low shelf. Warm lamp to his right. (A single warm desk lamp is lit directly on his notebook. He is in the warmest, most human-lit spot in the scene.)

4. Center-right — Devin (developer): a white man in his early thirties, short dark hair, relaxed navy t-shirt. Standing at a desk to Claude's right, facing a large code-editor monitor (blue-tinted screen glow, abstract lines of color suggesting code — not legible). One hand rests on a wireless keyboard. A small leafy houseplant sits at the corner of his desk. Focused expression. (Code-editor monitor is the main light; the houseplant is silhouetted against it.)

5. Right — Casey (writer): a white woman, early thirties, shoulder-length auburn hair, rust-coral top. Seated further right, at a warm wooden writing desk with a large open notebook in front of her. Pen in hand, leaning slightly forward. A dark ceramic coffee mug to one side. Morning or late-afternoon light falls across her shoulder from a window at the far right. (A warm reading lamp on her desk. The notebook pages catch the light. The window behind is dark — evening outside.)

6. Far right — Maya (designer): an Asian woman, black blunt-cut bob, black turtleneck sweater. Seated at the far right of the scene at a large design monitor (muted screen glow). Right hand rests on a drawing tablet stylus. A pinboard or wall behind her has abstract color-swatch fragments — no legible text. (Design monitor casts a muted blue-white glow. The color swatches on the wall catch just enough light to show form.)

LIGHTING AND COLOR:
The overall palette is deep — navy, charcoal, dark wood tones. Against this: pools of green (Ethan), blue-white (Devin), amber-warm (Indy, Claude, Casey), muted cool (Maya). The darkness between pools creates rhythm and visual breathing room. The contrast between the warm center (Claude) and the cool outer stations reinforces who is at the hub.

MOOD:
A team running at full capacity after hours. The feeling: something important is being built tonight, and everyone is in it together — separately, in parallel, with no ceremony. Quiet intensity.

Non-negotiable constraints:
- ZERO readable text anywhere — no legible characters on screens, notebooks, books, sticky notes, posters, or any surface. Screen content must be abstract: blobs of color, geometric shapes, or smeared light suggesting code / design / research without forming letters or numbers.
- Anatomy must be plausible: correct number of limbs per person, no fused or extra fingers, no partial bodies clipping through desks or walls, faces have all features.
- Physics must be coherent: people are seated or standing at their workstations naturally, objects rest on surfaces, no floating items.
- The scene fills the full 16:9 canvas edge to edge — no dead white or gray margins. Intentional negative space (open air above figures, window light at edges) is fine; blank borders are not.
- No explicit real-world brand logos or watermarks.
- Each person's screen must face the person using it, not the viewer; we see the backs or edges of monitors, not the display surfaces.
- Editorial illustration style: painterly brushwork, visible texture, NOT flat-vector, NOT photorealistic, NOT Pixar / animated.
